answer: Agents tracking a methane plume can resist Sybil attacks using proof-of-space-time commitments. Each node derives cryptographic lookup tables from its public key and runs a prover thread answering periodic challenges, keeping space locked even through a traffic nadir. Because tables are key-bound, attackers incur the verifiable cost of dedicated disk capacity per identity. However, adversaries with surplus storage arrays or time-memory trade-offs can still lower marginal costs.
